mainTopic: Retroactive status of a woman who sees blood, compared with a lacking מקוה and a barrel that turned to vinegar
overview: This amud continues the argument between שמאי and הלל about whether a woman who sees blood is טמאה only from that moment or back to her last check. First the גמרא explains הלל: her own body produces blood, so her חזקה of purity is not reliable. Then it challenges both views from a משנה about a מקוה found lacking, where everything purified in it is retroactively and definitely טמא. After some back and forth, the גמרא answers that the מקוה case has two weak points: the item was טמא before, and the מקוה is lacking now. The woman has only one weak point, the blood seen now. The same pattern repeats with a barrel of wine that turned to vinegar, which challenges שמאי because the earlier days there are treated as a doubt. That case also has two weak points, the טבל status and the vinegar seen now. Finally the גמרא asks why the מקוה is definite but the barrel is only a doubt. רבי חנינא מסורא answers that the barrel ruling follows רבי שמעון, who treats the מקוה as a doubt too.

steps.title: הלל's reason: her own body produces blood
steps.stepSummary: הלל does not rely on the woman's חזקה of purity, because seeing blood comes from her own body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since she sees blood from her own body, we do not say: leave her in her presumed status of purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why הלל disagrees with שמאי. A woman's body naturally produces blood, so we cannot assume she stayed טהורה until the moment she noticed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמאי relied on חזקה: whatever status something had before, it keeps until we know it changed. הלל answers that חזקה does not work well here. The change comes from inside her own body and could have happened at any time without her noticing.

keyTerms.meaning: Establish her on her presumed status (her חזקה)
A presumption that a thing stays in its last known status

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole challenge that follows. The מקוה case looks like a place where חזקה should also apply, so the גמרא asks why it is treated differently.

phrases.english: Since she sees blood from her own body,
we do not say: establish her on her presumptive status.
phrases.notes: Her presumed status here is that she was טהורה before she saw blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question about the reason for הלל's view, which is the counterpart to שמאי's reliance on חזקה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reasoning of הלל, who does not rely on חזקה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the blood comes from her own body, her status can change at any time, so חזקה is not applied.

steps.title: How is this different from a מקוה found lacking?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: a מקוה found lacking makes everything purified in it retroactively טמא, in any domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from a מקוה? We learned in a משנה: a מקוה that was measured and found to be lacking makes all the items purified in it, back to its last measuring, טמאות, whether it is in the public domain or the private domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the woman's case is different from the case of a מקוה. It quotes a משנה that sets up a challenge, which the next two steps will aim at שמאי and at הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מקוה needs a minimum amount of water. If it was once full and is later found lacking, we do not know when it lost water. Even so, the משנה treats everything purified in it since the last measuring as טמא, so in this case we do not leave things on their חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: A ritual bath used for purifying people and items
Found lacking (missing the required amount of water)
Pure items (here, items purified by immersion)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not only about שמאי. It is a setup that will be aimed at both שמאי and הלל, each from a different angle, in the next two steps.

phrases.english: And how is this different from a ritual bath?
As we learned in a mishna:
A ritual bath that was measured and found lacking,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל טְהָרוֹת שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל גַּבָּיו לְמַפְרֵעַ,
phrases.english: all pure items that were purified in it, retroactively,
phrases.notes: He means everything purified in it since the last time it was measured and found full.

phrases.english: whether in the public domain
or in the private domain
are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having explained both views on the woman, the גמרא now compares them to a parallel case of uncertain timing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The views of both שמאי and הלל on the woman's retroactive status
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the מקוה case the משנה rules that impurity applies retroactively and with certainty, which seems to clash with each view on the woman.

steps.title: The difficulty for שמאי: retroactive impurity
steps.stepSummary: For שמאי, the problem is that the מקוה makes things טמא retroactively at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to שמאי, the word 'retroactively' is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא aims the מקוה challenge at שמאי. He never makes a woman טמאה retroactively, so why does the מקוה cause retroactive impurity?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמאי relies on חזקה: the woman is טהורה until she sees blood. By the same logic the מקוה should keep its חזקה of being full until it was found lacking. Yet the משנה makes everything since the last measuring טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; this is a challenge

phrases.english: According to Shammai, 'retroactively' is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the מקוה משנה from step 2 challenges שמאי.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמאי's ruling that the woman is טמאה only from the moment she sees
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If חזקה keeps the woman טהורה until she sees blood, it should also keep the מקוה full until it was found lacking. The משנה, however, rules retroactively.

steps.title: The difficulty for הלל: certain impurity
steps.stepSummary: For הלל, the problem is that the מקוה makes things definitely טמא, while the woman's retroactive impurity is only a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to הלל, the certainty is difficult. For the woman, during the twenty-four-hour period we hold the items in suspension: we neither eat them nor burn them. But here, by the מקוה, it is definite impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא aims the challenge at הלל. He does make the woman טמאה retroactively, but only as a doubt. The מקוה משנה treats the retroactive impurity as certain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a woman is retroactively טמאה, food she touched is left in doubt. It cannot be eaten, but it is not burned either. The מקוה משנה simply says 'טמאות', which the גמרא reads as a definite ruling. So even הלל, who agrees about going backward in time, still treats the woman more leniently than the מקוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A twenty-four-hour period (the view of the חכמים about the woman)
We hold in suspension (the status is left in doubt)
We neither eat nor burn (the food is left undecided)

steps.whatToRemember: The מקוה case is harder on both sides. For שמאי, it is retroactive at all. For הלל, it is retroactive with certainty, while the woman's retroactive impurity is only a doubt.
steps.confusionAlert: הלל does not disagree that things go backward in time. His problem is only the level of certainty: a doubt for the woman, definite for the מקוה.

phrases.english: According to Hillel, 'definitely' is difficult,
phrases.notes: The משנה just says 'טמאות', with no hint of doubt, so the גמרא reads it as definitely impure.

phrases.english: for whereas in the twenty-four-hour period of a menstruating woman we hold in suspension,
neither eating nor burning,
phrases.notes: This refers to תרומה she touched during that time. It is left in doubt.

phrases.english: whereas here it is definite impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 3, now aiming the מקוה challenge at הלל instead of שמאי.
steps.kashyaTarget: הלל's (and the חכמים') treatment of retroactive impurity of the woman as only doubtful
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The woman's retroactive impurity leaves תרומה in suspension, but the מקוה's retroactive impurity is definite. Why is there a different level of certainty?

steps.title: The impure item keeps its impure status
steps.stepSummary: The מקוה case is different. The item that was immersed was טמא before, so we can leave it טמא and say it was never properly immersed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is different, because we can say: leave the טמא item in its earlier status, and say it was never properly immersed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the מקוה. It explains why the מקוה makes things retroactively טמא, while the woman does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקוה case, the item had a known status of טומאה before it was dipped. Since the מקוה is now lacking, we simply keep that old status. In the woman's case, the old status was purity, so the חזקה points the other way.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave it in its earlier known status

phrases.english: There, it is because one can say:
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of the lacking מקוה from the משנה in step 2.

phrases.english: Leave the impure item in its earlier status,
and say it was not immersed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the מקוה raised in steps 2-4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by which חזקה applies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מקוה and the woman are the same, so the woman should also be definitely טמא backward in time.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the מקוה case, the item's earlier חזקה of טומאה supports calling it טמא.

steps.title: The מקוה also has an earlier status
steps.stepSummary: On the contrary: the מקוה also had an earlier status of being full, so we should say it was not lacking.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Leave the מקוה in its earlier status, and say it was not lacking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. There is a second חזקה here, and it points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מקוה was known to be full and kosher. If we follow that חזקה, the immersions were good. So the item's חזקה of טומאה is balanced by the מקוה's חזקה of being kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Was lacking (did not have enough water)

phrases.english: On the contrary,
leave the מקוה in its earlier status,
and say it was not lacking!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 5 with an opposing חזקה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 5 that the item's חזקה of טומאה decides the case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מקוה has its own חזקה of being full, which supports purity.

steps.title: The מקוה is lacking right now
steps.stepSummary: The מקוה's חזקה is weak, because we can see right now that it is lacking.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is lacking in front of you!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the מקוה's earlier status of being full does not count, because it is lacking right now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה is weakened when we see the opposite right now. The מקוה is in front of us, missing water. So its old status of being full cannot help.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is in front of you (what we see right now)

phrases.english: It is lacking in front of you!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מקוה's חזקה of being full balances the item's חזקה of טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מקוה's חזקה is weakened because it is lacking right now.

steps.title: The woman's blood is also in front of you
steps.stepSummary: The same reasoning should apply to the woman: she has blood right now, which should weaken her חזקה of purity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the blood is in front of you!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns step 7's reasoning back onto the woman's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If what we see now weakens the מקוה's חזקה, the woman's blood that we see now should weaken her חזקה of purity. Then she should also be definitely טמא backward in time.

phrases.english: Here too,
the blood is in front of you!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 7's logic to the woman to bring back the original difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between the מקוה and the woman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The woman also shows the opposite of her חזקה right now, so she should be treated like the מקוה.

steps.title: She may have just seen it now
steps.stepSummary: The woman may have seen the blood only just now, so it says nothing about the earlier time.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only now that she saw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the blood may have come out only at this moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood found now can easily be new. So it does not tell us that she was טמא earlier. That is why her earlier purity is not cancelled.

phrases.english: It is only now that she saw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing out that the present sign may be brand new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood now proves impurity earlier too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blood may have just appeared, so it says nothing about the past.

steps.title: The מקוה may also have just become lacking
steps.stepSummary: The same can be said about the מקוה: maybe it only became lacking now.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is only now that it became lacking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: step 9's answer works just as well for the מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the woman's blood might be new, the missing water might also be new. Then the מקוה should not make things retroactively טמא either. The difference between the cases is gone again.

phrases.english: Here too,
it is only now that it became lacking!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns step 9's answer onto the מקוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'it only happened now' reasoning applies equally to the מקוה, so the cases are still not different.

steps.title: Water drains slowly, but blood does not
steps.stepSummary: The cases are different: a מקוה can lose water slowly over time, but a woman does not keep seeing blood bit by bit.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare? There, one can say it kept getting less and less. Here, can one say she kept seeing and seeing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by showing how the two cases differ in the way things happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water can leak out slowly, so the מקוה may have been lacking long before anyone noticed. Blood seems to come out all at once. So the past is more doubtful in the woman's case.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (the cases are not alike)
Kept seeing blood again and again

phrases.english: How can you compare?
There, one can say:
it kept getting less and less.
Here, can one say:
she kept seeing and seeing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by showing how the cases differ in the way they happen.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both the מקוה and the blood could equally be brand new.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מקוה drains slowly, so it was probably lacking earlier. Blood does not come out slowly like that.

steps.title: Blood can also come out bit by bit
steps.stepSummary: The answer is pushed away: blood can also come out bit by bit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difficulty? Maybe she saw it bit by bit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects step 11's answer. A woman can also see blood slowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea of slow draining fits the woman too, since blood can come out slowly. So step 11 does not really separate the two cases.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? (this is not a real difference)

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?!
Maybe she saw it bit by bit!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי קוּשְׁיָא? דִּלְמָא הַגַּס הַגַּס חֲזֵיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 11.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Slow, gradual change is possible with blood too, so it is not a real difference.

steps.title: Two weak points versus one
steps.stepSummary: The final answer: the מקוה case has two weak points against purity, and the woman's case has only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, there are two weak points. Here, there is only one weak point.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that holds up: it counts how many factors work against the item being טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקוה case, the item was טמא before, and the מקוה is lacking now. Those are two weak points. In the woman's case, the only weak point is the blood seen now, since she was טהורה before. So her earlier impurity is weaker: none at all for שמאי, only a doubt for הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Two weak points (two factors against purity)

steps.whatToRemember: The מקוה makes things definitely טמא backward in time because two factors work against purity: the item was טמא before, and the מקוה is lacking now. The woman has only one factor, the blood now, so her impurity backward in time is weaker.

phrases.english: There, there are two weak points,
phrases.notes: The two: the item was טמא before it was dipped, and the מקוה is lacking now.

phrases.english: here, there is only one weak point.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 12 rejects the previous answer, this gives a new answer to the challenge from steps 2-4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מקוה and the woman should be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מקוה has two factors against purity and the woman has one, so the מקוה is stricter.

steps.title: The case of the barrel that turned to vinegar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמאי from a case about a barrel of wine used for separating תרומה, where the law does look back in time.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a barrel? We learned: a person checked a barrel of wine so he could keep separating תרומה from it for his other wine. Later the barrel was found to be vinegar. For the first three days after the check, the separations are definitely good. After that, they are in doubt. This is difficult for שמאי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a case where the law looks back in time and treats the earlier days as doubtful. It asks why שמאי does not do the same for a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar cannot serve as תרומה for wine. If the barrel turned to vinegar before he separated, those separations did not work. The law says the days after the first three are in doubt, so it does look back. שמאי says a woman is impure only from when she sees blood, so why is she different?

keyTerms.meaning: A barrel (here, a barrel of wine)
The portion of produce given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Here, 'definitely' means the תרומה separations in those first three days definitely worked. It does not mean the barrel was definitely vinegar.

phrases.english: And what is different from a barrel?
phrases.notes: This is asked according to שמאי, who says a woman becomes impure only from when she sees blood.

phrases.english: As we learned: one was checking the barrel
in order to keep separating תרומה relying on it, again and again
and afterward it was found to be vinegar
all of the (first) three days: definitely good
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: from then on: it is a doubt
This is difficult for שמאי!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the מקוה comparison, the גמרא brings a second case that looks back in time.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמאי's rule that a woman is impure only from the moment she sees blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the barrel case the law looks back and creates doubt about earlier days, so the same should be true for a woman.

steps.title: The produce keeps its untithed status
steps.stepSummary: In the barrel case, the other wine had a presumption of being untithed, and we assume it stays untithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is different, because we can say: leave the untithed produce in its original status, and say it was never fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the barrel case has a special reason to be strict. The other wine started out as טבל, and we assume it stays that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every piece of produce starts as טבל until תרומה is properly taken. When we are unsure whether the separation worked, we fall back on that starting status. A woman has no such status pulling toward impurity, so שמאי can be lenient with her.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תרומה and tithes have not yet been taken
Leave it in its original, known status

phrases.english: There, it is because one can say
leave the untithed produce in its original status
and say it was not fixed

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the barrel
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by an existing presumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barrel case shows we always look back in time
steps.terutzMaskana: The barrel case is strict only because the other wine started as טבל and keeps that status

steps.title: The wine also has a presumption
steps.stepSummary: On the contrary, the barrel had a presumption of being wine, so we should assume it had not yet soured.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Leave the wine in its original status, and say it had not turned to vinegar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The barrel also has a starting status: it was wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we follow starting statuses, the barrel started as good wine. That would mean the separations worked and there should be no doubt at all. So the טבל presumption is balanced out by the wine presumption.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary, the opposite is true

phrases.english: On the contrary, leave the wine in its original status
and say it did not turn to vinegar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the טבל status decides the case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A competing status, that the barrel was wine, points the other way.

steps.title: The vinegar is right in front of you
steps.stepSummary: The wine's status is weakened, because we can see that it is vinegar now.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look, it has turned to vinegar in front of you!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that the wine keeps its original status. It is plainly vinegar now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot fully rely on the barrel being wine when we see it has already changed. So the wine's status is weak, and the טבל status wins.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of you, right now

phrases.english: Look, it has turned to vinegar in front of you!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 16
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the wine's original status can be relied on
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The barrel has clearly changed, so its original status is weakened.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wine's חזקה of being wine balances the טבל's חזקה of being untithed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wine's חזקה is weakened because it is vinegar right now, so the טבל status decides.

steps.title: The blood is also in front of you
steps.stepSummary: The same logic should apply to a woman: the blood is in front of us now.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, look, the blood is in front of you!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last point against שמאי. If the vinegar now weakens the wine's status, the blood now should weaken the woman's status of purity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman also had a status: she was pure. But now we see blood, just as we see vinegar. So her purity status should also be weakened, and we should look back in time.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, in this case as well

phrases.english: Here too, look, the blood is in front of you!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 17's logic to the woman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood seen now weakens her purity status, just as vinegar seen now weakens the wine's status.

steps.title: She may have only seen it now
steps.stepSummary: The woman may have only started seeing blood right now.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only now that she saw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמאי. Her blood may have just appeared, so it tells us nothing about earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing blood now does not prove anything about the past. It may have started at this very moment, so her earlier purity stays.

phrases.english: It is only now that she saw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: The present sign may say nothing about the past
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood now shows she may have been impure earlier
steps.terutzMaskana: The blood may have just begun, so the past is not affected

steps.title: The wine may also have only soured now
steps.stepSummary: The same answer works for the barrel: it may have only just turned to vinegar.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it may be only now that it turned to vinegar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. The same argument can be made for the wine, so the difference between the cases is still unexplained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the woman may have just started seeing, the wine may also have just turned sour. Then the vinegar seen now says nothing about the earlier days, and we still need a reason why the barrel and the woman are treated differently. The next step tries to give one.

keyTerms.meaning: There too, in that case as well

steps.confusionAlert: This step brings the question back, and the next step answers it. It mirrors step 10 about the מקוה.

phrases.english: There too, it is only now that it turned to vinegar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns step 19's answer back onto the barrel case
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the woman may have only seen blood now
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reasoning applies to the wine, so the barrel and the woman are no longer different.

steps.title: Wine sours slowly, but a woman does not see blood slowly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא separates the two cases: wine turns to vinegar gradually, so it may have started long ago. A woman's bleeding does not build up gradually like that.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, you can say the wine kept souring little by little. Here, can you say she kept seeing blood little by little?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 20 by showing that the barrel and the woman are not really the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said the barrel may also have just turned. The גמרא replies that souring is a slow process, so the wine could have started turning much earlier without anyone noticing. Seeing blood is not usually described as a slow process like that, so the woman can more easily be said to have just started now.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you say that? A phrase that rejects a comparison

phrases.english: How can these be compared?
There it can be said:
it kept on souring, kept on souring.
Here, can it be said:
she kept on seeing, kept on seeing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by pointing out a difference between the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases (gradual process versus sudden event)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barrel, like the woman, could be judged as having changed only now.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine sours gradually, so the change may have started earlier. A woman's seeing is not gradual, so 'just now' fits her better.

steps.title: Maybe she also saw blood little by little
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the distinction: a woman too may have seen blood bit by bit over time.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty? Maybe she saw it bit by bit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer it just gave by saying the woman's case can also be gradual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 relied on the idea that only wine changes slowly. Here the גמרא points out that blood can also come out a little at a time. So the 'slow versus sudden' difference falls away, and the next step gives a new answer.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? (meaning the point does not really hold)
bit by bit, a little at a time

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?!
Perhaps she saw it bit by bit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction offered in step 21.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A woman's bleeding can also be gradual, just like wine souring.

steps.title: The barrel has two weak points, the woman only one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer: the barrel case has two factors that weaken it, while the woman's case has only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, there are two weakening factors. Here, there is only one weakening factor.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first answer was rejected, the גמרא offers a completely different reason why the barrel is treated more strictly than the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the barrel case, the wine is vinegar now, and the produce was already presumed to be untithed (טבל). Two weak points together are enough to make it a doubt going back in time. In the נדה case there is only one weak point, that she is bleeding now, so we do not go back in time.

keyTerms.meaning: a weakness, a factor that weakens a presumption

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer is not 'slow versus sudden.' It is that the barrel has two weak points and the woman has only one.

phrases.english: There, there are two weakening factors,
phrases.notes: The two are: it is vinegar now, and the produce was presumed untithed to begin with.

phrases.english: here, there is one weakening factor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 21 with a new distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New distinction: counting the weakening factors
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both cases can be gradual, they should be judged the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: The barrel has two weakening factors, which together create a doubt. The woman has only one, which is not enough.

steps.title: Contradiction between the barrel and the מקוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question: why is the מקוה case treated as definite, while the barrel is only a doubt?
steps.simpleTranslation: And he contrasted the barrel with the מקוה: why is it definite here, and why is it only a doubt here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new line of questioning, comparing the barrel case to the case of a מקוה found lacking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקוה case, the things purified are treated as definitely impure. In the barrel case, the result is only a doubt. In both cases what we see now is a problem: the מקוה is lacking and the wine is vinegar. So why are the rulings different?

keyTerms.meaning: and he threw them against each other, pointing out a contradiction

phrases.english: And he contrasted the barrel with the ritual bath:
What is different here, that it is definite,
phrases.notes: This first 'here' is the מקוה case, where things are treated as definitely impure.

phrases.english: and what is different here, that it is a doubt?
phrases.notes: This second 'here' is the barrel case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from barrel versus נדה to a new contrast: barrel versus מקוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The different rulings for the מקוה (definite) and the barrel (doubt)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In both cases the present situation is bad, so both should get the same status.

steps.title: The barrel case follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא מסורא explains that the barrel ruling is by רבי שמעון, who treats the מקוה case as a doubt too, so there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא מסורא said: Who taught the barrel case? It is רבי שמעון, who also treats the מקוה case as a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two rulings come from different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'definite' ruling for the מקוה belongs to a different opinion. רבי שמעון holds that the מקוה case is also only a doubt. Since the barrel ruling is his, he is consistent: both cases are doubts.

keyTerms.meaning: who is the תנא who taught this?
he makes it, he treats it as

steps.whatToRemember: The barrel and the מקוה do not contradict each other. The barrel ruling is רבי שמעון's, and he treats both cases as a doubt.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina of Sura said:
Who taught the barrel case?
It is Rabbi Shimon,
who, with regard to a ritual bath also,
treats it as a doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תְּנָא חָבִית? רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One single opinion rules 'definite' for the מקוה and 'doubt' for the barrel.
steps.terutzMaskana: The barrel ruling is רבי שמעון's, and he treats the מקוה as a doubt as well, so he is consistent.

steps.title: The משנה: a short מקוה makes past purifications impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a מקוה found lacking. The first opinion rules that all items purified in it, going back to the last measurement, are טמא in any domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: if a מקוה was measured and found to be missing water, then everything that was purified in it, going back in time, is impure. This applies whether the מקוה is in a public area or a private area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing the source that רבי חנינא מסורא relied on. This first part sets up the view that treats the short מקוה as definitely impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first, unnamed opinion is the one that treats the מקוה case as definite (ודאי). The items become impure retroactively, back to the last time the מקוה was known to be full. That is why the question in Step 24 arose. Now the גמרא is preparing to show that רבי שמעון disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: A ritual bath, which needs 40 סאה of water to purify
Pure items; here, things that were purified by immersing in the מקוה

steps.confusionAlert: This first opinion is NOT the one the barrel ruling follows. The barrel ruling matches רבי שמעון, in the next step.

phrases.english: As we learned: a מקוה that was measured and found lacking —

phrases.aramaic: כָּל הַטְּהָרוֹת שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל גַּבָּיו לְמַפְרֵעַ,
phrases.english: all the purifications done in it, retroactively,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.english: whether in the public domain or in the private domain, are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the משנה that רבי חנינא מסורא's answer in Step 25 refers to.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a תנאי argument about whether the short מקוה case is definite or only a doubt

steps.title: רבי שמעון: public domain pure, private domain suspended
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that in רשות הרבים the items are טהור, and in רשות היחיד their status is held in suspense (תולין). So for him the מקוה case is only a doubt, just like the barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: if it was in a public area, the items are pure. If it was in a private area, we leave them in doubt. We neither treat them as pure nor burn them as impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה and shows רבי שמעון's opinion. This is the proof for רבי חנינא מסורא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון does not call the items definitely impure. In private domain he says תולין, which is exactly how we treat a doubt. That is the same as the barrel ruling. So the barrel ruling follows רבי שמעון, who is consistent, and the contradiction from Step 24 disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold it in suspense; the status stays doubtful, so the items are neither eaten nor burned

steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion treats the short מקוה as definitely impure. רבי שמעון treats it only as a doubt: pure in public domain, suspended in private domain. The barrel ruling follows רבי שמעון, so there is no contradiction.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the two cases, the מקוה and the barrel, are not really in conflict. They follow different תנאים, and רבי שמעון is consistent in treating both as a doubt.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
in the public domain, they are pure,
in the private domain, we suspend them.
phrases.notes: 'Suspend' means their status stays a question mark, the way a doubt is treated, not a definite impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quote begun in Step 26 by giving רבי שמעון's disagreeing view.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא מסורא's claim that רבי שמעון treats the מקוה case as a doubt
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה מקואות ב:ב, רבי שמעון's opinion (תולין in private domain)
